title: Biomarker-Based Precision Dentistry: Current Evidence, Clinical Translation, and Future Directions in Personalized Oral Healthcare
html: Purpose of Review Precision dentistry aims to integrate molecular biomarkers into clinical decision-making, enabling personalized prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment of oral diseases. Although many biomarkers have been identified, their use in dentistry is limited. This review critically assesses the evidence supporting biomarker-based precision dentistry, highlighting its clinical applicability, implementation challenges, and future directions for translating molecular diagnosis into personalized oral health care. Recent Findings Recent advances in multi-omics and multiplex technologies, biosensors, microfluidic platforms, liquid biopsies, artificial intelligence (AI), and point-of-care (POC) diagnostics have improved biomarker detection and analysis in oral cancer. Inflammatory, oxidative stress, genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, metabolic, and microbiological biomarkers have great potential for the early screening, diagnosis, risk stratification, prognostic evaluation, and treatment of periodontal disease, peri-implant disease, oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), dental caries, and pulpal disease. However, most biomarkers remain in the exploratory or validation phase, and only a relatively small number have sufficient evidence to guide routine biomarker-based therapeutic decisions. Summary Biomarker-based precision dentistry is an important step towards predictive, preventive, and individualized oral health care. However, biological variability, a lack of standardized analytical protocols, limited multicentre validation, regulatory barriers, reimbursement issues, and cost-efficiency concerns still limit its widespread implementation. Future progress will depend on robust clinical validation, evidence-based guidance, interdisciplinary cooperation, and mainstreaming validated biomarker platforms into routine practice. Graphical Abstract A schematic representation of biomarker-based precision dentistry, translational framework and clinical implications. Biological sources, biomarker classes, and diagnostic technologies support integrated biomarker discovery and subsequent clinical application, implementation, and personalized care. The framework also summarizes the anticipated clinical impact, key implementation challenges, and future priorities required for reliable translation into dental practice.
